subtitle: Year 8 Civics Revision
description: Agorian. Year 8 Civics and Citizenship revision for the Democracy in Action unit. Challenge what you know.
ogDescription: Year 8 Civics and Citizenship revision for the Democracy in Action unit. Quick questions with explanations, scenario practice, a timed challenge and flashcards for the key terms.

units.name: Democracy and government
units.blurb: Democracy, the Constitution, three levels and three branches of government, parties and Parliament.
units.topicsNote: Democracy in Action, Power in Australia, Parties, Policies and Power

units.name: Citizens and participation
units.blurb: Citizenship and national identity, rights and responsibilities, and how to have your say.
units.topicsNote: Many Stories, One Australia and Have Your Say!

units.name: Laws and justice
units.blurb: What makes a law effective, and fairness, equality and access in the justice system.
units.topicsNote: Effective Laws and Justice for All

hero.text: The agora was the open square of Athens where citizens traded, voted and were questioned by Socrates. This is yours. Quick questions with an explanation after every answer, scenario practice, a timed challenge and flashcards for the key terms, all across the Democracy in Action unit.
hero.alt: Raphael's fresco The School of Athens, philosophers in debate under a great arch
hero.cap: Raphael, The School of Athens, 1511. Athenian thinkers arguing in a great hall. Athens is where the word democracy, rule by the people, was born.

welcome.lead: An additional revision tool. Finish the revision booklet first, then test yourself here.
steps: Three times, do one Scenario practice. Read the scenario twice, answer the four questions, read every explanation.
Twice, do Multiple-choice practice on the topics under 70 per cent in Your progress by topic.
Once, try Challenge, then an Interactive and Key terms for anything you blanked on.

modes.title: Multiple-choice practice
modes.blurb: Pick topics, answer at your pace, read the explanation after every question. Word-bank gaps are mixed in.

modes.title: Scenario practice
modes.blurb: Seven scenarios you have not seen. Read one, then answer four quick questions with explanations.

modes.title: Challenge
modes.blurb: 20 questions from the whole unit against a 10 minute clock. On your own, or with a class code so everyone gets the same 20.

modes.title: Key terms
modes.blurb: Flashcards to flip, a ten-definition sprint against the clock, and Explain it in 25 words.

modes.title: Interactives
modes.blurb: Sort real responsibilities, pass a referendum, form a government, fix a law, spot the errors. Seven things to try.

verdicts: Test ready on these topics. Try a scenario next.
Solid. Read the explanations on the ones you missed and go again.
Getting there. Practise the weak topics below before the next challenge.
Early days. Pick one topic at a time in Multiple-choice practice and build it up.

links.title: Trusted sites
links.intro: Official and well-established sources on how Australia's democracy works. Use them to check a fact or read further. They open in a new tab.
